An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).

130	- **Never route an `error` port back into the happy path** — an error edge into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failed run report `Completed` with success-shaped outputs. Send it to a distinct End node with an error/status output, to `core.logic.terminate`, or to a branch that genuinely recovers.
131	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
132	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
133	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
134	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
135	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
136	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
137	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
138	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
139	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
140	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
141	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
142	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
143	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
144	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
145	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
146	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
147	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker. Strip it and pass a `=js:` expression returning the array (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": "=js:(['a', 'b'])"`). Never a literal JSON array — it validates but does not bind. 7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->
45	
46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.

111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.

113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. 139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. 145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {

152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"

156	  }

260	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
264	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:end-->
265	
266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py` and `scripts/flow_compose.py` parse the file and rewrite the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. One call per node, edge, variable, or composite rewrite — see [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for the per-operation flags. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
301	
302	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
303	
304	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

320	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
321	
322	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
323	
324	```bash
325	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
326	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
327	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
328	```
329	
330	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
331	
332	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
333	
334	Chain `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py "<ProjectName>.flow"` into the same call, before `validate` — it reports the defects `validate` does not catch (wiring, `=js:` fields, Jint constructs, resource bindings, runtime gaps) while you are still in T3.

336	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
337	
338	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). 3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.switch`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Switch node for multi-way branching (3+ paths) based on ordered case expressions. Cases are evaluated in order; the first `true` case is taken.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Switch? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Three or more paths based on different conditions | Yes |
16	| Simple true/false branch | No — use [Decision](../decision/planning.md) |
17	| Branch on HTTP response status codes | No — use [HTTP](../http/planning.md) built-in branches |
18	| Branch requires reasoning on ambiguous input | No — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input` | `case-{id}` (dynamic per case), `default` |
25	
26	## Key Inputs
27	
28	| Input | Required | Description |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| `cases` | Yes | Array of `{ id, label, expression }` (min 1 item) |
31	
32	Each case creates a dynamic output port: `case-{item.id}`. An optional `default` port handles unmatched cases.

35	
36	- Switch nodes produce one outgoing edge per case + optionally one from `default`
37	- Each case edge uses `sourcePort: "case-{id}"` where `{id}` matches the case's `id` field

"description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 5	## 1. Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix
6	
7	The `uip` CLI is installed via npm. Resolve the binary (it may not be on PATH in nvm environments) and detect the command namespace.
8	
9	```bash
10	UIP=$(command -v uip 2>/dev/null || echo "$(npm root -g 2>/dev/null | sed 's|/node_modules$||')/bin/uip")
11	CURRENT=$($UIP --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}')
12	```
13	
14	If `uip` is not found at all, install it:
15	
16	```bash
17	npm install -g @uipath/cli@latest
18	```

20	If `npm install -g` fails with a permission error, prompt the user to re-run with appropriate privileges — do not retry automatically.

24	| Installed version | Command prefix | Example |

26	| **≥ 0.3.4** | `uip maestro flow` | `uip maestro flow init MyProject` |

41	## 2. Always use `--output json`
42	
43	All `uip` commands support structured JSON output. Use `--output json` whenever output is parsed programmatically — every reference doc and recipe in this skill assumes it.

45	```bash
46	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
47	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
48	uip maestro flow instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
49	```

55	## 3. Prefer `--output-filter` for extraction
56	
57	When extracting one field or a projection from `uip --output json`, use `--output-filter '<jmespath>'`. The CLI exposes `--output-filter <expression>` as a global flag on every subcommand; it applies a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) expression to the `Data` envelope **before** printing. Write expressions starting at `Data` — do **not** prefix them with `Data.`.
58	
59	**Canonical example (broad discovery)** — list all nodes matching a keyword with the standard projection:
60	
61	```bash
62	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
63	  --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
64	```
65	
66	This is the form used in the connector skill — see [Cross-references](#cross-references) below — and is the right starting point when you want to inspect what's available.
67	
68	**Narrow query** — once you know the connector namespace, filter to a single connector's activities:
69	
70	```bash
71	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
72	  --output-filter "[?starts_with(NodeType,'uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-slack.')].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName}"
73	```
74	
75	`registry search` returns `Data` as a **flat array of PascalCase objects** — `NodeType`, `Category`, `DisplayName`, `Description`, `Version`, `Tags`, `AvailableOnTenant`. Not `Data.Nodes`, not lowercase `type`/`category`; those shapes do not exist. Knowing the shape lets you write the right expression on call #1 — which is the actual protection. Do **not** rely on `--output-filter` to *catch* a wrong-shape guess: a syntactically valid expression that simply doesn't match (e.g. `--output-filter "Nodes"` or `"Nodes[*].NodeType"` against the flat array) returns `Data: []` with **exit 0** — the same silent trap as `python3`/`jq` (see the silent-`[]` note below). Only an *invalid* expression fails loudly with exit 3: a syntax error, or a type error such as `keys(@)` on an array.
76	
77	> **Never `head`/`tail`/`grep -m`/pager a discovery query** (`registry search`, `is connectors list`, any `list`/`search`). A row past the cutoff reads exactly like a row that doesn't exist — the same false-absence trap as the silent `[]`, self-inflicted. To check existence, push the predicate into `--output-filter` so the result is *all* matches and already small; cap rows only on data already known complete or already filtered.
78	>
79	> ```bash
80	> uip … registry search slack --output json --output-filter "[?contains(NodeType,'get-channel-info')].NodeType"   # right: every match
81	> uip … registry search slack --output json --output-filter "[*].{…}" | head -100                                # wrong: hides matches past line 100
82	> ```
83	
84	### When to fall back to `python3` / `jq`
85	
86	`--output-filter` is the preferred extraction mechanism, but it is not a general-purpose transformation tool. Fall back to `python3 -c` or `jq` when JMESPath cannot express the operation:
87	
88	- Multi-step joins across two CLI calls.
89	- Format conversion (JSON → CSV, JSON → env-var assignments).
90	- Conditional output that depends on a value computed from multiple fields.
91	
92	Before reaching for an external parser, verify the JSON shape. The CLI roots `--output-filter` expressions at `Data`, so:
93	
94	- **Check whether `Data` is array or object first** — `--output-filter "type(@)"` returns `"array"` or `"object"`. `keys(@)` throws on arrays (`Filter 'keys(@)' failed to evaluate: Invalid type: keys() expected argument 1 to be type (object) but received type array instead`), so use `type(@)` as the first probe.
95	- **If `type(@)` returned `"object"`:** `--output-filter "keys(@)"` lists the top-level field names at `Data`.
96	- **If `type(@)` returned `"array"`:** `--output-filter "[0]"` shows the first row, or `--output-filter "[0] | keys(@)"` lists the keys of one row.
97	- **Watch for silent `[]`** — when the JMESPath path doesn't match anything, the CLI returns `Data: []` with `Result: "Success"`. That's the exact silent-failure mode the docs are designed to surface. If you got `Data: []` and were expecting a value, double-check field-name casing — **and note casing differs by command:**
98	  - `registry search` / `list` (and most `uip … --output json` commands) return **PascalCase** keys → filter `[*].NodeType`, `[*].DisplayName`.
99	  - `registry get` returns the node definition **verbatim** (it is pasted straight into the `.flow`), so its keys keep the manifest's own casing — predominantly **camelCase**: `Node.nodeType`, `Node.inputDefinition`, `Node.supportsErrorHandling`, `Node.form.sections[…]`. A few nested *runtime-output* schemas are PascalCase because the engine emits them that way (e.g. Summarize's `content.Text` / `content.Citations`) — match whatever the manifest actually declares, not a normalized form.
100	  - When unsure, probe before guessing: `--output-filter "keys(@)"` (object) or `--output-filter "[0] | keys(@)"` (array).
101	
102	Most agent-side retry loops on `uip --output json` parsing come from guessing the shape wrong; verify, then parse.
103	
104	### Cross-references
105	
106	The broad-discovery recipe above is used in [author/references/plugins/connector/planning.md](../author/references/plugins/connector/planning.md) (§ Discovery) for connector discovery and [author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for connection-resource lookup. Keep the three in sync on the **preference** (always `--output-filter`) and the **shape pin** (`registry search` Data is a flat array of PascalCase objects); each file may pick a projection appropriate to its task.
107

109	
110	Every `uip` command returns one of two response shapes:
111	
112	**Success:**
113	```json
114	{ "Result": "Success", "Code": "FlowValidate", "Data": { ... } }
115	```
116	
117	**Failure:**
118	```json
